name: Ab Rauf Yusoh
_note: M2 state-executive cohort (Phase 2). Chief Minister of Melaka (13th) since 31 Mar 2023, after Sulaiman Md Ali resigned. Added as a BN-aligned executive to balance the class. Provisional Layer B anchors pending the blind panel (minCodersToScore=3). Citations search-corroborated; reconfirm against primary sources. A5 none-on-record: his only court matter is one he initiated as plaintiff (a defamation suit); graft cases in Melaka involve other officials, not the CM. B4 and B5 left unscored (the Akmal exco matter is a personnel decision not a policy U-turn; the deviant-teachings statement touches belief).

metrics.justification: No criminal charge, MACC investigation, or conviction against Ab Rauf personally is on record; his only court matter is one he brought as plaintiff (a defamation suit in which the Melaka High Court granted him an injunction in September 2025), and graft cases surfacing in Melaka involve other officials. Recorded as the subject's own status: none on record.

citation.title: Melaka CM granted injunction in defamation suit against Bersatu leader

metrics.justification: After Kampung Lubok Kasau was flooded three times between March and April 2025, he announced (July 2025) a RM1.5 million flood-mitigation project, deepening Sungai Bemban and raising a 2.2km embankment to protect over 300 villagers, with works scheduled to finish by November 2025. A documented, dated mitigation response (anchor 2).

citation.title: Flood-prone Kg Lubok Kasau to get RM1.5mil flood mitigation project, says Melaka CM

metrics.justification: Visit Melaka Year 2024 exceeded its target: arrivals surpassed the 8.7 million goal by end-September and reached 12.32 million from January to October 2024, a measurable tourism-recovery delivery (a higher full-year total he cited is the state's own unaudited figure). Delivered against a stated target (anchor 3).

citation.title: TMM2024: Melaka Records 12.32 Mln Visitors From January To October

metrics.justification: His administration established the Melaka Youth State Assembly (announced May 2024) as a standing youth-governance institution; its first session swore in 34 youth members across all portfolios, and he committed that its proposals would feed into the 2026 state budget. A dated, repeatable institution-building mechanism (anchor 3).

citation.title: Melaka to establish Youth State Assembly for enhanced youth involvement in governance
